```

This uses `>=`. If `byte_index + length_of_length == bytes_max`, we go to the error path. But what if `byte_index + length_of_length > bytes_max`? We also go to the error path.

In the error path, `byte_index` is unchanged (returned by `ptls_asn1_error_message`). `*decode_error` is set. `*last_byte` is still `bytes_max` (set at line 139).

Then back in `ptls_asn1_validation_recursive`:
- `last_byte = bytes_max`
- `last_byte <= bytes_max` = true
- structure_bit = 1
- while loop: `byte_index < last_byte` = `byte_index < bytes_max`

But `byte_index` is the value returned by `ptls_asn1_read_length`, which is the same as the input `byte_index` (since the error path doesn't change it). So `byte_index < bytes_max` is true (since `byte_index` was less than `bytes_max` when we entered `ptls_asn1_read_length`).

The while loop executes. The recursive call has `last_byte - byte_index = bytes_max - byte_index > 0`. No crash.

But wait, what if `byte_index` is `bytes_max - 1`? Then `last_byte - byte_index = bytes_max - (bytes_max - 1) = 1`. The recursive call has `bytes_max = 1`. No crash.

What if `byte_index` is `bytes_max`? Then `last_byte - byte_index = bytes_max - bytes_max = 0`. But `byte_index < bytes_max` is false, so the while loop doesn't execute. No crash.
